source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Carrollton campus publishes 45 MW of IT load capacity across 600,000 square feet of technical space, representing 9.5% of Texas's disclosed data center capacity and ranking third in the state by published megawatt figures.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this facility could accommodate roughly 1,125 racks. At 8 H100-equivalent accelerators per rack, a standard configuration, that scales to approximately 9,000 accelerators if the full IT load were deployed to GPU compute. The campus certifications span PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942 Tier standards, qualifying it for regulated workloads across finance, healthcare, and government sectors.

The 45 MW figure is published capacity, not currently deployed or committed allocation. The operator's public spec page does not disclose how much space is occupied, what tenant mix presently occupies the building, or whether any capacity is reserved for AI workloads. The physical infrastructure and compliance posture exist to host substantial GPU clusters, but the gap between available power and actual accelerator deployment remains opaque. Texas shows 133 mapped facilities total, yet only 19 publish capacity figures, meaning most of the state's data center footprint remains unmeasured on this metric.
